hypothesis: The cost/selectivity order derived on a frozen development distribution preserves exact AND semantics but can become more expensive than the naive order under a bounded transfer of probability mass from a learned-order early-reject state to a learned-order late-reject state.
learned_order_rule: Sort ascending by exact Fraction(predicate_cost, development_false_probability), ties by predicate name.
truth_space: All 16 Boolean assignments, generated in lexicographic A,B,C,D order with false before true.
drift_grid: 0 through the development probability mass of the source state, inclusive, in 10 equal Fraction-valued increments. Subtract each delta from source and add it to destination.
metrics: exact semantic AND agreement for all states
audit: Separate standard-library-only implementation; recompute from this freeze and raw state rows, without importing producer code. Two copied-evidence corruption controls: alter a cost and alter a semantic outcome; auditor must reject both.

decision.pass: PASS_DRIFT_BOUNDARY_MAPPED if exact reconciliation holds, both corruption controls reject, and first crossover or no-crossover-on-grid is identified.
decision.fail: FAIL_SEMANTIC_OR_COST_RECONCILIATION on any semantic or independent cost mismatch.
decision.hold: HOLD_DRIFT_GRID_INSUFFICIENT if frozen source/destination mass endpoints are absent or crossover cannot be resolved at frozen grid resolution.
decision.stop: STOP_SOURCE_IMAGE_OR_AUDIT if exact cached image/source/audit gate unavailable.

limits: Authored finite distribution and fixed cost units only
Per-row percentiles are not end-to-end latency
No real predicate/provider latency, GUI behavior, authority, online drift detector, optimality, or runtime/product benefit claim
